title: fix(app-shell): hold a server refusal against the draft slice it named
body:
Fixes #8057

## What was wrong

`metadata-admin`'s `ResourceEditPage` is a third metadata writer, reached by neither guard objectui#7714 landed: `doSave` serialises the draft and calls `client.save(type, name, body, { mode: 'draft' })` directly, routing through neither `toFieldsMap`.

Measured against a real 17.3.0 backend: add a Lookup field with an empty target and every subsequent auto-save PUTs the same half-filled document and takes the same 422 — while the designer renders later edits as applied and the server holds none of them. The only escape was a page reload, which discards every unsaved edit since.

## Which mechanism carries the invariant, and why it survives a selection change

The existing block, `inspectorBlocking` (`:696` on `83d4fda16`, still `:696` on this base), is stamped `blockingReport.key === selectionKey`, so it expires when the selection changes — which **is** step 2 of the reproduction. Widening that stamp is not the fix: a selection-scoped term cannot carry a document-scoped invariant.

So this adds a **second, document-scoped term beside it** rather than stretching the existing one. `saveRefusal` records a refusal the **server returned** and holds it against the draft **slice** its issue path named. It has no selection in it at all, which is why it survives step 2.

Kept separate from `issues` on purpose: that state is overwritten wholesale by the debounced live Zod pass 200ms after any edit, so a server verdict parked there is gone by the author's next keystroke — part of why this wedge was silent.

### The slice is the PARENT of the refused path, and that is load-bearing

`fields.lookup.reference` is held against `fields.lookup`. The commonest refusal is a missing required key, whose own value is absent **by definition** — that absence is why the server refused. Keying on the path itself would compare `undefined` with `undefined` on every later render, so the block could never release: a dead-bolt. The parent is present, and it moves both when the author fills the key in and when they delete the element outright. Both are real escapes; keying on the path has neither.

A refusal that localises to **no** slice holds nothing. Fail-open is deliberate: an unlocatable refusal names nothing the author could edit to clear it.

## The advisory carve-out, written and pinned on both halves

    server-REFUSED   BLOCKS     (refusalBlocking)
    server-ACCEPTED  advisory   (unchanged)

This does **not** narrow objectui#4306 / objectui#6980, and the distinction matters. That ruling is about a verdict the client **predicts**, and its stated reason is that the client may be stricter than the server — so blocking would dead-bolt Save "on a draft the server accepts". `refusalBlocking` is armed only by a 422 the server actually returned, so it cannot be armed by a draft the server accepts: there is no refusal to arm it with. The dead-bolt stays unreachable, and no prediction was promoted to a block.

Both docblocks were amended so no two rulings in the tree contradict each other, and each suite names the other.

## Evidence

Every pin was observed to fail. Four ablation legs, each mutating a **read site** from a committed tree, proved on disk in both directions (anchor counts + `git hash-object` vs the HEAD blob + a line-total gate), restored by state (`git diff HEAD` empty), classified per test from vitest's JSON reporter. All five death strings counted **0** on every leg, so these are assertion failures, not suites failing to load.

| Leg | Mutation (read site) | Red | Reads as |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | the caricature — `refusalBlocking` always non-zero ("Save is always blocked") | **9** incl. **both pre-existing advisory pins** | the advisory half reddens loudly |
| B | key the block on the whole document instead of the named slice | **3** | the near-miss that blocks and still fails the two wedge tests |
| C | fix removed (`refusalBlocking` always 0) | **4** | the pre-fix tree |
| D | fail-open guard dropped (hold unlocatable refusals) | **1** | the dead-bolt pin is live and isolated |

Leg B is the sharpest: an implementation that **does** block — passing the advisory half, the control, the release path and the settled-refusal path — is still caught by exactly the two tests that encode the measured wedge.

**The discriminating pin**: *Save stays blocked after the selection moves off the offending element*. Reusing `inspectorBlocking` as-is fails only that one.

**The non-regression axis**, derived from the plausible wrong fix ("block Save on any Zod issue"): the load-bearing cases are the server-**accepted** issues that must still save, and they are observed on a document the server really takes — `client.save` resolving, not a button merely looking enabled.

Every negative assertion carries a **lit control** that fires the same call on the same harness with the refusal absent.

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/` — **244 files, 2553 passed**, 1 skipped, exit 0
- `turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/app-shell` — exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`)
- `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` — OK, 6857 files
- `node scripts/check-designer-field-key-parity.mjs` — OK
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — OK

All at `03ba75f88`.

## Fences honoured

Not strip-and-report-saved (objectstack#4001 — the refused content is never dropped). Not `check-designer-field-key-parity.mjs` (untouched; a missing `reference` is a failed refinement, which its own boundary section excludes). Not a port of the objectui#7714 guard (there was nothing to copy). `MetadataFieldsPage` is untouched — objectui#8058 / objectui#8060 are a different writer and a different mechanism.

## Is there a fourth writer? Yes — there are nine more, and the obvious sweep cannot see them

⚠️ **The prescribed sweep shape is itself unsound, and I measured that on this card's own subject.** A sweep for `client.save(` returns **zero hits in `ResourceEditPage.tsx`** — the file this card is about — because the call is `client.save<any>(`. There is also a second, entirely different method spelling: `client.meta.saveItem(`, which is how one of the two writers the ruling *did* name actually writes.

    # population proved live first (lit control: `doSave`, 10 files)
    git grep -ln 'doSave' -- 'packages/*/src/*' 'apps/*/src/*'
    # both spellings, non-test, non-comment
    { git grep -n '\.save[<(]'      -- 'packages/*/src/*' 'apps/*/src/*';
      git grep -n 'meta\.saveItem(' -- 'packages/*/src/*' 'apps/*/src/*'; } \
      | grep -v '\.test\.' | grep -vE ':[0-9]+: *(\*|//|/\*)' | grep -vE '\* ' \
      | grep -E "'object'|\((type|parentType|current\.type)|save<" | sort -u
    git grep -n 'toFieldsMap' -- 'packages/*/src/*' | grep -v '\.test\.'

Population 3962 + 191 files. Result: **15 object-metadata write call sites across 10 files**. `toFieldsMap` guards **3 of them, in 2 files** — the two writers the ruling named. **Twelve call sites across eight files** route through neither guard; this PR fixes one.

The unguarded remainder: `EmbeddedItemEditor.tsx:120` · `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx:755` · `DatasourceResourcePage.tsx:427` · `runtime-metadata-persistence.ts:207,314` · `PackageOwdOverviewPanel.tsx:252` · `StudioDesignSurface.tsx:1886,2988,3010,3053` · `MetadataObjectsPage.tsx:257`.

⚠️ Measured: they do not route through the guards. **Not** measured: whether any of them actually emits a refused body. Reported as an observation, not asserted as a defect.
